BiblicalUsage: Pishteh is linen, the thread carded from flax into cloth. Rahab hid the spies under stalks of flax on her roof in Joshua 2:6, and the priests of Ezekiel's temple wore linen garments in Ezekiel 44:17. The law forbade a garment of wool and linen together in Deuteronomy 22:11.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that linen on a priest and flax on a roof both tell the same story — God uses plain things for holy work.
